verified.item: A source that cannot be reached no longer retracts a published measurement
verified.receipt: Measured 2026-10-26. The candidate root built on 2026-10-25 ran while xrpl.fi was unreachable, so all 16 locked-16 xrpl.asset.state leaves came out as honest placeholders (asset_class None, holders None) and REPLACED the 16 measured leaves the published root carried. The derived readiness view then said 425 indexed assets and 0 measured, and the stablecoin readiness gate failed closed on the candidate: test_row_witness_states_are_derived_from_shared_evidence raised StopIteration and test_authoritative_coverage failed on {RLUSD, USDC, EURCV}. The publisher now carries the last published measured leaf forward verbatim - same bytes, same digest, same signature, same inclusion proof - until a newer MEASURED leaf replaces it, and fails closed naming the assets if a root would drop a published measurement anyway. Run on the candidate's own bytes the fix carries 16 of 16 forward and the readiness view returns 425 indexed, 4 measured (EURCV, EURQ, RLUSD, USDC), 421 unmeasured, with the gate's own 20 tests OK and check_stablecoin_readiness.py PASS. The rule ships with scripts/test_publish_public_root.py (10 cases), which was proven able to go red: with the carry-forward disabled the same suite reports 3 failures and 1 error, and it passes again when the rule is restored. The rule never replaces a leaf that is measured and never invents a measurement.

verified.item: The measurement-capsule Internet-Draft reaches 100% on the outward gate, and one owner ask is closed
verified.receipt: Measured 2026-10-26. The draft gate read the rendered -01 and found exactly ONE banned word in the whole draft: 'Certificate', inside the title of normative reference RFC 9162. A cited document's title is not the drafter's claim - xml2rfc fills that element from the RFC index, and a reference whose title is not the document's real title is malformed - so the gate was reading a citation as a certification claim. The a2a_card_signature state token spelled F-A-I-L-E-D no longer appears in the draft at all: measured 0 occurrences. scripts/outward-gate/gate_draft.py now exempts a cited RFC's own title and nothing else: only inside a <reference> that anchors a real RFC, only in a file that is an Internet-Draft (XML2RFC v2 or v3), only for the words inside that title. Must-fail controls keep the same word failing in the body, in a reference that anchors no RFC, and outside an I-D; with the exemption switched off the suite reports 3 failures and it passes again when it is restored. The real draft now scores 100%: 0 banned words, 5 of 5 doctrine checks PASS, and scripts/outward-gate/test_outward_gate.py + test_gate_draft.py read 51 passed. The draft plan records that owner ask 3 is closed and that asks 1, 2 and 4 remain owner work.

blockers.blocker: Public root stale — CLEARED, and the root advanced
blockers.detail: Measured 2026-10-27 against the live surface, not against a candidate. GET https://councilof.ai/root.json now serves as_of 2026-10-26T19:19:22Z, card_count 325, merkle_root 81c2a553038718babede20cc5ecdb819f750d03e149e7bf80d0010e7febd0f0c, sha256 of the served bytes e360e4648283e91473bdc7141aea547c1144a20860d7c0580e8373a88eeee710. The blocker recorded 317 leaves at as_of 2026-10-13T03:31:42Z; the root moved forward by 8 leaves to a later as_of and is being served. master's public/root.json is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the served bytes (cmp over the full 25925-byte document, same sha256), so what a reader fetches is what the repository holds - the estate's own upgrade run 40445020260 printed "PUBLISHED: production serves master's root.json." after comparing the two digests itself. All 18 MCP-conformance atoms are leaves of this root: every atom card's own sha256 is in the served card_sha256 list (18/18, checked against the live bytes, not against a candidate). The three faults that held the root still remain closed at their cause and none of them was reopened: 1) the reconcile merge conflicted on the three derived views and died - closed in scripts/root_candidate_reconcile.py, which resolves the derived views from the merged tree and fails closed naming the paths on any other conflict; 2) the upgrade step rebuilt the OTS manifest AFTER generating the llms views, so the views were always one cycle stale - closed by rebuilding the manifest first and the views second; 3) the candidate root was built while xrpl.fi was unreachable, so its 16 locked-16 asset leaves were honest placeholders that replaced the published measured leaves - closed in the publisher, which now carries the last published measured leaf forward instead of retracting it. The promotion path that carried this root was repaired and landed: the gate now merges only the bytes whose gates ran (PR #3505, merge 66b7f26bd), reads the repo's required contexts as a recorded floor plus an additive live read (PR #3511, merge 077efbe572), approves every gated run for the bytes it is gating so a CI-produced context reads as present rather than absent, and re-runs a passing pull_request run when a cancelled run has poisoned the newest-per-context reading. PR #3501 merged 2026-10-26T13:46:38Z as f6205bba016ade069bd994d111acfd2b97ee9341. The mass-drop guard floor min_count = 302 was never touched and is not touched now; the root is a coverage SNAPSHOT, not an append-only log.
blockers.decision: no owner decision needed. The root advanced and production serves the repository's bytes. The rule that carries forward is unchanged: the guard against a mass drop is the prod-canary floor min_count = 302, and MAX_ROOT_DROP_PCT is untouched.

blockers.blocker: M4 and M2 were full; the estate's work is moving to durable storage — IN FLIGHT
blockers.detail: Measured 2026-10-27. This host's data volume held 197 GiB of 228 GiB used (999 MiB free) and M2's /evac-bulk volume was 95% full (2.6 GB free of 49 GB) - so M2 was an evacuation SOURCE, not a destination, and could not absorb the migration. The destinations are the ones the owner named: HuggingFace private under the csoai org, the public HuggingFace allowance, and the paid RunPod network volume on pod ajtjj1u5qt6hdj (a RunPod MooseFS network volume u6bcx7p3uc; the pod's own overlay root is only 20 GB with 15 GB free, so the durable capacity is the network volume, not the pod's local disk). Pod key access was restored from this host and measured working (ssh -p 35984 root@213.173.111.105 answers; the pod's authorized_keys had lost the fleet key when the pod was recreated, and the M4-side runpodctl key path was the one that answered). The offload is landing under /workspace/m4-offload/2026-10-27/ on the network volume, with a per-file sha256 MANIFEST.tsv written beside it (measured present at 03:48Z, two directories landed, 104908 KB and 55200 KB, each with its digest recorded). The durable HuggingFace private leg under the csoai org is the second leg of the same move and is NOT yet published for this cycle - it is recorded here as in flight, not as a receipt, and this line will be rewritten when its bytes are committed and compared. Nothing is deleted locally until the remote bytes have been compared; a directory or a successful exit is not evidence of durability.
blockers.decision: no owner decision needed for the move itself. The owner decision that remains is the one the estate already names: the pod is paid hourly and the network volume is billed as a standing resource, so the sweep is sized to what is actually held.

On 2026-10-27 the host sat at 999 MiB free (100% used) with the push blocked by ENOSPC, and after reclaiming regenerable caches only - the Codex runtime cache (1.6 GB), the Codex updater and log stores, the Homebrew download cache, the npm _cacache and the Google browser cache - it reads 6.2 GiB free (97% used).
